issues.legal_issue: For a specific-performance suit, a contractual event that makes the performance date ascertainable fixes the date from which limitation runs, even when the agreement states no calendar date.
material_facts: The agreement required the defendant to execute and register a sale deed when the plaintiff redeemed the mortgaged property and took possession of the registry papers.
The plaintiff redeemed the mortgage in 1970, making the agreed performance date ascertainable.
The plaintiff demanded performance by notice in July 1984 and brought the suit more than three years after the redemption.
The trial court and High Court held the suit was not barred because no calendar date or deadline for redemption had been specified.
issues.conclusion: The date for performance was fixed by reference to the redemption event, and limitation began when the plaintiff redeemed the mortgage. Because the suit was filed after the limitation period had elapsed, it was barred; the appeal was allowed and the suit dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 54 of the Limitation Act, 1963, the limitation period for specific performance runs from the date fixed for performance, or, if no date is fixed, from when the plaintiff has notice that performance is refused. The date need not be stated as a calendar day in the agreement if its basis is stated and the event makes it certain. The agreement was a contingent contract under section 31 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, enforceable when the event occurred; the doctrine id certum est quod certum reddi potest applied. The Court relied on R. Muniswami Goundar v. B.M. Shamanna Gouda and Duncombe v. The Brighton Club and Norfolk Hotel Company, and distinguished Sathula Venkanna v. Namuduri Venkatakrishnayya, Kruttiventi Mallikharjuna Rao v. Vemuri Pardhasaradhirao, and Kashi Prasad v. Chhabi Lal.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and contract_sets_performance_on_ascertainable_event and event_occurred and suit_brought_after_limitation_from_event

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement.
predicates.contract_sets_performance_on_ascertainab: The agreement makes performance due upon an event whose occurrence makes the performance date ascertainable.
predicates.event_occurred: The event that makes performance due occurred.
predicates.suit_brought_after_limitation_from_event: The suit was brought after the applicable limitation period had elapsed from the event that made performance due.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit concerns an agreement making performance due upon an ascertainable event, and the event occurred before the suit was brought after the applicable limitation period elapsed, the suit is barred by limitation.
